exact_claim_text: (1) For prime p == 1 (mod 6) and n, r >= 1, a(n*p^r - 2) == -A005717(n-1) (mod p), where we take A005717(0) = 0 to match Batalov's conjecture above.
semantic_summary: For p congruent to 1 modulo 6 and n,r>=1, the Motzkin number a(n*p^r-2) is congruent to -A005717(n-1) modulo p.

exact_claim_text: 8. The primes in the sequence appear in their natural order.
semantic_summary: Prime values occur in increasing prime order in the Yellowstone permutation.

exact_claim_text: A stronger conjecture: for every n there exists a number k < 1 + n^(.75) such that n*k + 1 is a prime.
semantic_summary: For every positive n, the least k with k*n+1 prime is less than 1+n^(3/4).

exact_claim_text: Although the description of the sequence defines it as "the smallest x" with a certain property, this is conjectured, not yet proven.
semantic_summary: The solution x of 127^x-113^x=1 is the least exponent for which q^x-p^x=1 for a pair of consecutive primes p<q.

exact_claim_text: Zhi-Wei Sun conjectured that for every n = 2,3,... the polynomial f_n(x) = Sum_{k = 0..n} binomial(n,k)^2 * binomial(2*k,n) * x^(n-k) is irreducible over the field of rational numbers.
semantic_summary: For every integer n>=2, Sun's polynomial f_n(x)=Sum_k binomial(n,k)^2*binomial(2k,n)*x^(n-k) is irreducible over Q.

exact_claim_text: Apparently Goldbach conjectured that any a > 1 from this sequence can be written as a=b+c where b and c are in this sequence (Lemmermeyer link below).
semantic_summary: Every a>1 with a^2+1 prime is a sum b+c where both b^2+1 and c^2+1 are prime.

exact_claim_text: Conjectural: a(n*p^k) == a(n*p^(k-1)) ( mod p^(3*k) ) for  prime p >= 5 and positive integers n and k.
semantic_summary: For A347854, a(n*p^k) is congruent to a(n*p^(k-1)) modulo p^(3k) for every prime p>=5 and positive n,k.

exact_claim_text: Conjecturally for every k>=2, as in the case k=1, the sequence (*) is a permutation of the positive integers.
semantic_summary: For every k at least 2, the generalized Yellowstone sequence defined in A247225 is a permutation of the positive integers.

exact_claim_text: Conjecturally, the number of sequences (e(1), ..., e(n+1)), 0 <= e(i) < i, such that there is no triple i < j < k with e(i) > e(j) <= e(k).
semantic_summary: A071356(n) counts inversion sequences of length n+1 avoiding triples i<j<k with e(i)>e(j)<=e(k).

exact_claim_text: Conjecture 1: a(n) equals the number of multiples of 4 whose representation in base 5/4 (see A024634) has n-1 digits.
semantic_summary: A120160(n) counts multiples of 4 having exactly n-1 digits in base 5/4.

exact_claim_text: Conjecture 1: Every number with at least two distinct prime factors is in the sequence.
semantic_summary: Every positive integer with at least two distinct prime factors occurs in the Enots Wolley sequence.

exact_claim_text: Conjecture 2: a(n) equals 1/5 times the number of nonnegative integers with the property that their 5/4-expansion has n digits (assuming that the 5/4-expansion of 0 has 1 digit).
semantic_summary: Five times A120160(n) is the number of nonnegative integers whose base-5/4 expansion has n digits.

exact_claim_text: Conjecture: (2/n)*Sum_{k=1..n} (2k+1)*a(k)^2 is an integer for each positive integer n.
semantic_summary: For every positive n, (2/n) times the weighted sum of squared Motzkin numbers is an integer.
Every nonnegative integer has at least one restricted four-square representation counted by A281976.

exact_claim_text: Conjecture: a(n) > 0 for all n > 1.
semantic_summary: Every integer n>1 can be written as x+y with x,y positive and x(x+1)/2+y^2 prime.

exact_claim_text: Conjecture: a(n) > 0 for all n > 2
semantic_summary: Every even integer 2n with n>2 is p+q for primes p,q such that the prime index pi(p) is also prime.

exact_claim_text: Conjecture: a(n-1) == 0 (mod n^4) for all n congruent to 1 or 5 mod 6
semantic_summary: For every n congruent to 1 or 5 modulo 6, A357512(n-1) is divisible by n^4.

exact_claim_text: Conjecture: a(n) != -1 for all n.
semantic_summary: For every cyclic group C_n, iterating the automorphism-group operation eventually stabilizes.

exact_claim_text: Conjecture: a(n)^(1/n) is a strictly decreasing function of n. Namely a(n+1)^(1/(n+1)) < a(n)^(1/n) for all n.
semantic_summary: The n-th roots of the lesser twin primes form a strictly decreasing sequence.

exact_claim_text: Conjecture: a(n) == 2 (mod n^3) iff n is prime.
semantic_summary: A positive integer n is prime exactly when its Franel number A000172(n) is congruent to 2 modulo n^3.

exact_claim_text: Conjecture: |a(n)| > 2*n^4 for all n > 2.
semantic_summary: For every n>2, the absolute value of Ramanujan's tau(n) exceeds 2*n^4.

exact_claim_text: Conjecture: a(n) is odd iff n is a term of A022341.
semantic_summary: A000139(n) is odd exactly when n is an odd fibbinary number in A022341.

exact_claim_text: Conjecture: a(n) = sqrt(12)^(n-Theta(log n)). - _Manfred Scheucher_, Aug 22 2016
semantic_summary: The minimum number of triangulations of an n-point planar set is sqrt(12) raised to n minus a Theta(log n) term.

exact_claim_text: Conjecture: |a(n)| with n > 1 can never be a perfect power.
semantic_summary: For every n greater than 1, the absolute Ramanujan tau value |tau(n)| is not a perfect power.

exact_claim_text: Conjecture: Every harmonic number is practical (A005153).
semantic_summary: Every harmonic or Ore number is a practical number.

exact_claim_text: Every multiply-perfect number is practical (A005153).
semantic_summary: Every integer n for which n divides sigma(n) is practical.

exact_claim_text: except for the number 3, a(n) are the numbers such that a(n)^2+2 are Lucas numbers.
semantic_summary: Apart from 3, the terms of A002878 are exactly the positive integers x for which x^2+2 is a Lucas number.

exact_claim_text: Conjecture: for a prime p > 5, p has primitive root 2 iff p == +-3 (mod 8) divides 2^k + 3 for some k < p - 1 and divides 2^m + 5 for some m < p - 1.
semantic_summary: For every prime p>5, 2 is a primitive root modulo p exactly when p is congruent to plus or minus 3 modulo 8 and divides suitable 2^k+3 and 2^m+5 with exponents below p-1.

exact_claim_text: Conjecture: For all m >= 0, there exists at least one possible value of n such that a(n) = m. - _Ahmad J. Masad_, Jan 06 2018
semantic_summary: Every nonnegative integer occurs as the number of unordered prime-pair decompositions of 2n for some n.

exact_claim_text: Conjecture: for all n>1, abs(a(n)-(n/log(n))) < sqrt(n). - _Alain Rocchelli_, Sep 20 2023
semantic_summary: For every n>1, the number of primes between n^2 and (n+1)^2 differs from n/log(n) by less than sqrt(n).

exact_claim_text: Conjecture: For any integers n >= m > 0, there are infinitely many integers b > a(n) such that the number Sum_{k=m..n} a(k)*b^(n-k) (i.e., (a(m), ..., a(n)) in base b) is prime
semantic_summary: For every finite block A001359(m),...,A001359(n), infinitely many bases larger than its last term make the block's base-b value prime.

exact_claim_text: In general, for any integer m>1 and n>0, the polynomial f_{m,n}(x) = Sum_{k=0..n} (m*k)!/(k!)^m*x^k is irreducible over the field of rational numbers.
semantic_summary: For every m>1 and n>0, the factorial-ratio polynomial sum from k=0 to n of (mk)!/(k!)^m times x^k is irreducible over Q.

exact_claim_text: Conjecture: For each k >= 0, there exists a minimum sufficiently large number r that depends on k such that for each n >= r, a(n) > k. - _Ahmad J. Masad_, Jan 08 2020
semantic_summary: The Goldbach representation count A045917(n) tends to infinity as n tends to infinity.

exact_claim_text: Conjecture: for r >= 2, and all primes p >= 5, a(p^r) == a(p^(r-1)) ( mod p^(3*r+3) ). - _Peter Bala_, Oct 13 2022
semantic_summary: For every prime p>=5 and r>=2, A352655(p^r) is congruent to A352655(p^(r-1)) modulo p^(3r+3).

exact_claim_text: Conjecture: for r >= 2, u(p^r) == u(p^(r-1)) ( mod p^(3*r+3) ) for all primes p >= 5. - _Peter Bala_, Oct 13 2022
semantic_summary: For the binomial expression u defined for integer parameters j and k, every prime p>=5 and r>=2 satisfies u(p^r) congruent to u(p^(r-1)) modulo p^(3r+3).
Every nonnegative integer is representable as u^3+v^3+2x^3+2y^3+3z^3 with nonnegative integers u,v,x,y,z and the stated ordering conventions.

exact_claim_text: Conjecture: if S is a (provable) Sierpiński number, then there exists a prime P such that S^p is also a Sierpiński number for every prime p > P. - _Thomas Ordowski_, Jul 12 2022
semantic_summary: Every provable Sierpiński number S has a threshold P beyond which S^p is Sierpiński for every prime exponent p.

exact_claim_text: Conjecture: let the smallest prime factor of Fermat number F(n) be P(F(n)). If F(n) is composite, then P(F(n)) < 3*2^(2^n/2 - n - 2). - _Arkadiusz Wesolowski_, Aug 10 2012
semantic_summary: Every composite Fermat number has smallest prime factor below the stated exponential bound.

exact_claim_text: Conjecture: Limit_{n->oo} n / PrimePi(a(n)) = 1/2. - _Alain Rocchelli_, Mar 17 2024
semantic_summary: Among primes, the weak primes have asymptotic density one half.

exact_claim_text: Conjecture: log log a(n+1) - log log a(n) < 1/n. - _Thomas Ordowski_, Feb 17 2023
semantic_summary: For every index n, the increment from log log p_n to log log p_(n+1) is less than 1/n.

exact_claim_text: Conjecture: No a(n) has the form x^m with m > 1 and x > 1. - _Zhi-Wei Sun_, Dec 02 2013
semantic_summary: No Bell number is a nontrivial perfect power.

exact_claim_text: Conjecture: Numbers n such that gcd(d+1, n) > 1 for every proper divisor d of n. Verified up to 10^696. - _David Radcliffe_, May 29 2025
semantic_summary: A014117 is exactly the set of n for which every proper divisor d satisfies gcd(d+1,n)>1.

exact_claim_text: Conjecture: Sequence = {5 and n <> 5| ( Fibonacci(n) mod n = 1 or Fibonacci(n) mod n = n - 1) and 2^(n-1) mod n = 1}. - _Gary Detlefs_, May 25 2014
semantic_summary: Apart from the separately included 5, an integer is prime exactly when it satisfies both the stated Fibonacci congruence and the base-two Fermat congruence.

exact_claim_text: Conjecture: sequence contains infinitely many pairs of twin primes. - _Benoit Cloitre_, May 08 2003
semantic_summary: Infinitely many twin-prime pairs consist of primes for which 2 is a primitive root.

exact_claim_text: Conjecture: The asymptotic limit of the average of log(a(n)) ~ log(log(prime(n))) - gamma (where gamma is Euler's constant). Also, for n tending to infinity, the geometric mean of a(n) is equivalent to log(prime(n)) / e^gamma. - _Alain Rocchelli_, Jan 23 2023
semantic_summary: The mean logarithm of prime gaps has the stated Euler-constant correction, equivalently their geometric mean is asymptotic to log(p_n)/e^gamma.

exact_claim_text: Conjecture: The equation |a(m)a(n)| = x^k with m < n, k > 1 and x >= 0 has no solution. This has been verified for m < n <= 5000. - _Zhi-Wei Sun_, Dec 29 2024
semantic_summary: No product of two distinct-index absolute Ramanujan tau values is a nontrivial perfect power.

exact_claim_text: Conjecture: the limit of X(n)/n = 1+1/t and limit of Y(n)/n = 1+t where the limit of Y(n)/X(n) = t = tribonacci constant (A058265), and thus the limit of (Y(n) + X(n))/(Y(n) - X(n)) = t^2 and the limit of (Y(n)^2 + X(n)^2)/(Y(n)^2 - X(n)^2) = t.
semantic_summary: The paired greedy-queens coordinates have linear growth constants determined by the Tribonacci constant, with the stated equivalent ratio limits.

exact_claim_text: Conjecture: the numbers > 5 in this sequence, i.e., 2^2^k + 1 for k>1, are exactly the numbers n such that (n-1)^4-1 divides 2^(n-1)-1. - _M. F. Hasler_, Jul 24 2015
semantic_summary: For n>5, n is a Fermat number exactly when (n-1)^4-1 divides 2^(n-1)-1.

exact_claim_text: Conjecture: The numbers |a(n)| (n = 1,2,3,...) are distinct. This has been verified for the first 10^6 terms. - _Zhi-Wei Sun_, Dec 21 2024
semantic_summary: The absolute values of Ramanujan's tau function are pairwise distinct.

exact_claim_text: Conjecture: The sequence is infinite (that is, a(n) always exists).
semantic_summary: Every term of the recursively defined Yellowstone sequence A254077 exists, so the sequence continues indefinitely.

exact_claim_text: Conjecture: there is a strengthening of the Bertrand postulate for n >= 24: the interval (n, 2*n) contains a safe prime. It has been tested by _Peter J. C. Moses_ up to n = 10^7. - _Vladimir Shevelev_, Jul 06 2015
semantic_summary: For every integer n >= 24, some safe prime lies strictly between n and 2*n.
A189281 satisfies the displayed degree-11, order-8 polynomial-coefficient recurrence.

exact_claim_text: Conjectures: 1) For k>=3, except for k=5, if a(n) = prime(k), then a(n-2) = 2*prime(k) and a(n+2) = 3*prime(k). This conjecture was verified by _Peter J. C. Moses_ for n <= 5000. - _Vladimir Shevelev_, Feb 09 2015. This conjecture verified for n <= 10^7. - _Ray Chandler_, Apr 02 2015. Extended to n <= 10^9. - _John Mason_, Jun 08 2016
semantic_summary: Except for prime(5), whenever A254077(n)=prime(k) with k>=3, the terms two places before and after are 2*prime(k) and 3*prime(k).

exact_claim_text: Cramer conjecture prime(n+1) - prime(n) < C log^2 prime(n) is equivalent to the inequality (log prime(n+1)/log prime(n))^n < e^C, as n tend to infinity, where C is an absolute constant. - _Thomas Ordowski_, Oct 06 2014
semantic_summary: For some absolute constant C, prime(n+1)-prime(n) is eventually less than C*log^2(prime(n)).

exact_claim_text: Erdős called a weak prime an "early prime." He conjectured that there are infinitely many consecutive pairs of early primes, and offered $100 for a proof and $25000 for a disproof (Kuperberg 1992). See A229832 for a stronger conjecture. - _Jonathan Sondow_, Oct 13 2013
semantic_summary: There are infinitely many pairs of consecutive primes that are both early or weak primes.

exact_claim_text: For the given initial values k, it is conjectural that their sequences S(k) never merge. The S(k) have been checked to be distinct for 2^60 terms (see Rowland link), but it is possible that they merge later on.
semantic_summary: For every listed initial value k, the gcd-add trajectory S(k) never merges with any trajectory from an earlier surviving seed.

exact_claim_text: Gilbert & Pollak conjectured that this is the Steiner ratio rho_2, the least upper bound of the ratio of the length of the Steiner minimal tree to the length of the minimal tree in dimension 2. (See Ivanov & Tuzhilin for the status of this conjecture as of 2012.) - _Charles R Greathouse IV_, Dec 11 2012
semantic_summary: The planar Steiner ratio equals sqrt(3)/2.

exact_claim_text: Hardy and Littlewood conjectured that the asymptotic number of elements in this sequence not exceeding n is approximately c*sqrt(n)/log(n) for some constant c.
semantic_summary: The count of integers k at most n for which k^2+1 is prime has the stated c*sqrt(n)/log(n) asymptotic in the pinned source.

exact_claim_text: Conjecture: If a(n) = 1, then a(2n+1) is not 0.
semantic_summary: If the Riesel-search stopping time A050412(n) equals one, then A050412(2n+1) is nonzero.

exact_claim_text: conjecture: also limsup(a(n) - A080359(n)) = infinity (cf. A182366). - _Vladimir Shevelev_, Apr 27 2012
semantic_summary: The limsup of the difference between the n-th Ramanujan prime and A080359(n) is infinite.

exact_claim_text: Conjecture: Sum_{p <= x, mu(p-1)=1} 1 = (A/2)*x/log x + o(x/log x) and Sum_{p <= x, mu(p-1)=-1} 1 = (A/2)*x/log x + o(x/log x).
semantic_summary: Primes with squarefree p-1 split asymptotically equally between mu(p-1)=1 and mu(p-1)=-1, each with density constant A/2.

exact_claim_text: Let C_n(R, H) denote the transition matrix from the ribbon basis to the homogeneous basis of the graded component of the algebra of noncommutative symmetric functions of order n. Letting I(2^(n-1)) denote the identity matrix of order 2^(n-1), it has been conjectured that the dimension of the kernel of C_n(R, H) - I(2^(n-1)) is always equal to a(n-1).
semantic_summary: The eigenspace of the ribbon-to-homogeneous transition matrix C_n(R,H) with eigenvalue one has dimension A001405(n-1).

exact_claim_text: Moll's conjecture 5.5 extends to this sequence and takes the form: for prime p == 1 or 3 (mod 8), the p-adic valuation v_p(a(n)) ~ n/(p - 1) as n -> oo.
semantic_summary: For every prime p congruent to 1 or 3 modulo 8, v_p(A363409(n)) is asymptotic to n/(p-1).

exact_claim_text: for any positive integer n, Zhi-Wei Sun conjectured that the polynomial P_n(x) = Sum_{k=0..n} a(k+1)*x^k is irreducible over the field of rational numbers with the Galois group S_n
semantic_summary: For every positive n, Sun's prime-coefficient polynomial P_n is irreducible over Q and has Galois group S_n.

exact_claim_text: in every arithmetic progression r (mod s) for arbitrary integral r and s, there are infinitely many integers n for which p(n) is odd
semantic_summary: Every integral residue class modulo every modulus contains infinitely many n for which the partition number p(n) is odd.

exact_claim_text: Ore conjectured that 1 is the only odd harmonic number.
semantic_summary: No odd harmonic divisor number greater than one exists.

exact_claim_text: Prime(n) is in the sequence if (and conjecturally only if) A133954(n) = prime(n). - _Vladimir Shevelev_, Aug 30 2013
semantic_summary: For p=prime(n), p has primitive root 2 if and only if A133954(n)=p.

exact_claim_text: [Stronger than Firoozbakht] conjecture: All (prime(n+1)/prime(n))^n values, with n >= 5, are less than n*log(n).
semantic_summary: For every n>=5, (p_(n+1)/p_n)^n is less than n*log(n).

exact_claim_text: Wolfgang Haken (1977) conjectured that no term of this sequence is a perfect square
semantic_summary: No integer formed by the first n+1 decimal digits of Pi is a perfect square.
